games.summary: The saved power and talent contributions both favor Rutgers, producing an outright upset projection. The quarterback change makes that unadjusted margin especially fragile.
games.availability_note: AJ Surace will start for Rutgers after Dylan Lonergan's injury (Sept 8 reporting). No player-specific adjustment is included in this frozen margin.

games.summary: Power and talent are the strongest contributors toward Missouri. The injury situation on both sides is a material counterargument, not a reason to invent a precise point adjustment.
games.availability_note: Missouri: Ahmad Hardy reported out; Malae Fonoti out for the season. Kansas: Bam Crouch doubtful and Cam Pickett a game-time decision. These reports are not quantified in the frozen projection.

games.summary: Power and talent favor Tennessee, while the portal-offense contribution pulls toward Georgia Tech. The model sees a Volunteers win, but a much closer game than the market does.

Nebraska's talent, power and portal-offense contributions all point toward a comfortable win. The moved line leaves very little cushion; a big projected win is not automatically a good big-spread pick.
The main contributions favor Tulsa outright, but the combined margin is well short of the market handicap. Sam Houston is a keep-it-close selection, not the projected winner.

Power and talent favor Tulane; coaching and replacement-burden contributions offset part of that advantage. The remaining spread disagreement is small enough that ordinary projection error can overwhelm it.
Power and coaching favor Kennesaw State, while the talent contribution favors Georgia State. This is a useful reminder that the pick is not simply taking the more talented roster.
Power and portal offense pull toward Marshall, with success-rate evidence pushing back. The model has the home favorite clearing the line, subject to the early-season sample warning.
UCLA's talent advantage is partly offset by power and replacement-burden contributions. The model still picks UCLA outright, but San Diego State gets enough points to be the ATS side.
Power and success-rate contributions favor Ohio State; the preseason-prior contribution pushes toward Texas. The result is an Ohio State upset projection, not just an underdog cover.
Power and talent strongly favor Texas Tech. Oregon State is strictly a spread selection: the model still expects a decisive Tech win, and the large-spread review remains important.
Power, talent and coaching favor Iowa, while portal offense partially offsets them. Iowa is the model's SU and ATS side; that does not eliminate rivalry-game or small-sample uncertainty.
Talent and power favor Clemson, but success-rate and preseason-prior contributions reduce the gap. Georgia Southern is the ATS side, with only a slim cushion after the line move.

The power contribution strongly favors Navy, while talent and portal offense push toward Florida Atlantic. That disagreement produces a narrow FAU upset projection and makes it a particularly fragile read.
LSU's talent and portal-offense contributions drive a large projected win; replacement burden pushes back. Louisiana Tech is the spread side, not an upset call. Large-spread uncertainty remains.

Talent, power and portal offense favor Auburn, with replacement burden tempering the margin. Southern Miss gets a sizable cushion versus that projection, but a large discrepancy is not validated ATS skill.
Power and talent drive an enormous Ole Miss margin. Charlotte is still the ATS side because the market asks for even more; late scoring and substitutions can decide a spread this large.
Power and coaching contributions favor North Dakota State. Its FBS-transition flag makes the comparison less reliable than an established FBS matchup, despite the model taking NDSU outright and ATS.
Power favors Utah while talent pushes toward Arkansas. The final margin is almost exactly the market number: this is a requested model selection with effectively no meaningful point cushion.
The projection favors Fresno State outright but is far tighter than the market. Sacramento State carries an FBS-transition flag; the unusually large gap should invite scrutiny, not extra confidence.
Power, talent and success-rate contributions all favor USC. The model lays the points, but the handicap remains large enough for substitution patterns and late scores to matter.
Power and talent favor Hawaii, with portal offense pulling the other way. The model projects a two-score win. This is Saturday evening in Hawaii, but midnight Sunday in Eastern time.
